questions.question: How do scientists calculate global surface temperatures to ensure accuracy?
options: By using a single highly advanced satellite orbiting the Earth.
By taking tens of thousands of temperature measurements worldwide.
By measuring temperatures only in major capital cities.
By averaging temperatures from the deepest parts of the oceans.

questions.question: When scientists analyse global temperature changes, what do they compare current regional temperatures with?
options: The long-term average temperature for that specific region.
The temperature of the nearest desert.
The global temperature recorded exactly one year ago.
The theoretical maximum temperature possible on Earth.

questions.question: What general trend has been observed in overall global surface temperatures since the industrial revolution in the 1850s?
options: They have remained completely stable.
They have been steadily decreasing.
They have been increasing.
They have fluctuated with no clear long-term direction.

questions.question: Which of the following can scientists study to get reliable data about temperature changes from hundreds or thousands of years ago?
options: Deep sea sand dunes and modern weather reports.
The movement of tectonic plates and active volcanoes.
Tree rings and ice cores.
Fossilised animal bones and coal deposits.

questions.question: What is the main environmental consequence of the increasing levels of greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere?
options: A decrease in global sea levels and cooler oceans.
Global warming and climate change.
The complete destruction of the ozone layer.
An increase in solar radiation reaching the upper atmosphere.

questions.question: How does methane compare to carbon dioxide as a greenhouse gas?
options: Methane is less potent than carbon dioxide.
Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Methane and carbon dioxide have the exact same warming effect.
Methane is only harmful when it reacts with carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is the primary effect of having greenhouse gases naturally present in Earth's atmosphere?
options: They keep the atmosphere warmer than it would be without them.
They block all heat from the Sun from reaching the Earth's surface.
They make the atmosphere much colder by reflecting sunlight.
They prevent any oxygen from escaping into space.

questions.question: Why does the melting of land-based ice sheets due to increased temperatures cause sea levels to rise?
options: It releases trapped air bubbles that push the water upwards.
It moves more water from the land into the sea.
Melting ice sheets decrease the density of seawater, making it take up less space.
The cold water from ice sheets causes ocean currents to speed up.

questions.question: Why does the melting of floating sea ice in the summer NOT raise sea levels?
options: Floating ice is already displacing its own weight of water, so melting it does not add water to the sea.
The melted sea ice immediately evaporates into the atmosphere.
Sea ice is made of fresh water which is less dense than sea water.
The melted ice is quickly absorbed by marine life.

questions.question: Apart from melting land ice, what is another major reason why global sea levels are rising?
options: Warmer oceans and seas expand in volume.
Increased rainfall directly fills up the ocean basins.
Undersea volcanic eruptions push water upwards.
Tides are becoming stronger and more frequent.

questions.question: Which of the following are produced when we burn fuels for transport?
options: Only carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Greenhouse gases, other pollutant gases, and particulates.
Pure oxygen and nitrogen gas.
Helium and non-toxic soot particles.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the emissions of petrol/diesel vehicles and electric vehicles?
options: Electric vehicles burn fuel directly, whereas petrol vehicles use electricity.
Neither petrol nor electric vehicles release any emissions.
Petrol and diesel vehicles burn fuels, while electric vehicles do not, though power stations may burn fuel to make their electricity.
Electric vehicles produce more tailpipe pollutants than diesel vehicles.

questions.question: How does carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology work?
options: It converts CO₂ into oxygen in the upper atmosphere.
It releases CO₂ into deep ocean currents to be diluted.
It separates CO₂ from other emissions and stores it in suitable deep underground locations.
It burns CO₂ at high temperatures to turn it into harmless ash.

questions.question: What is a major drawback of using carbon capture and storage technology despite its ability to reduce CO₂ emissions?
options: It causes an increase in local sulfur emissions.
It is very expensive to implement and run.
It only works during the summer months.
It requires the use of radioactive materials.

questions.question: Roughly what percentage of global greenhouse gas emissions is produced by the energy sector?
options: Around 10%
Around 25%
Around 50%
Around 75%

questions.question: Under what conditions will a car use more energy to travel a distance of 100 km?
options: If the car is lighter or travels at lower speeds.
If the car is heavier or travels at higher speeds.
If the car is painted a darker colour.
If the car travels during the night.

questions.question: How does maintaining the correct air pressure in car tyres affect energy use?
options: It causes the car to use less energy.
It has no effect on the energy consumed by the car.
It increases the energy needed because of increased friction.
It only saves energy when driving downhill.

questions.question: Why will renewable energy resources not run out?
options: They are stored in infinite underground tanks.
They are replenished more quickly than we use them up.
They do not release any energy when used.
They are created by chemical reactions in the Earth's core.

questions.question: How is a turbine spun to generate electricity when burning fuels like biomass, oil, or gas?
options: By using the direct force of falling ashes.
By using moving steam produced by burning the fuel.
By using the gravitational pull of the fuel.
By using the wind generated by cooling fans.

questions.question: Which of the following technologies produces electricity without needing an electric generator with a spinning turbine?
options: Wind turbines
Hydroelectric dams
Coal-fired power stations
Solar panels
